text:
alex_k: Quick sync — putting together the on‑prem/VPC launch playbook. Want to lock scope and acceptance tests before the PRD goes final.

maria_s: good call. Is this covering customer-managed egress + cert handoff?

alex_k: yes — three focus areas: 1) network handshake (BGP/NAT/egress IPs), 2) control plane reachability & auth (KMS, certs), 3) operational runbook (deploy, rollback, escalation).

sam_devops: Can we add an explicit golden path for egress? Many customers expect static IPs or NAT mapping. Suggest: "egress golden path" + fallback: proxy through our regional relay.

chris_net: +1. Also need to call out DNS split‑horizon and customer FW expectations. Add acceptance: customer provides an L3 contact and a validated BGP session test.

nisha_pm: For product prioritization — if a customer can't support BGP, what minimal scope do we accept to still ship? Is IPsec tunnel + NAT okay? Need to define beta vs GA.

alex_k: Proposed tiers in PRD: Beta = IPsec/MPLS tunnel with static NAT; GA = direct BGP peering with advertised egress range. Acceptance criteria for beta: working traffic flow at 100rps for 15m, validated TLS termination, logs forwarded. GA adds automated BGP health checks and failover time <30s.

sam_devops: Add KMS note: customers may require customer‑managed keys (CMK) in their HSM. Acceptance: ability to rotate certs without downtime (hot swap). Workflow sample:

```bash
# validate cert rotation sequence (local)
curl -X POST https://controlplane.example/internal/rotate-cert 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' 
  -d '{"customer_id":"cust-123", "new_cert":"---BEGIN CERT---"}'
```

maria_s: Nice. Also add monitoring SLIs we will require from the customer: control plane ping, BGP session state, egress health endpoint (200 OK).

chris_net: Edge cases to call out: asymmetric routing, overlapping CIDRs, customer NAT re-use. For each: list mitigation and test steps. Example mitigation for overlapping CIDR = prefix translation; acceptance = successful iptables rule applied in staging.

alex_k: I'm drafting an ops checklist section — onboarding 3 steps: 1) network handshake window (2h), 2) smoke tests (connectivity + auth), 3) production cutover + post-cutover monitoring (1h). Who owns the handshake?

sam_devops: Platform oncall owns step 1 & 3. Customer success owns scheduling + runbook during the window. Add explicit rollback trigger: >10% error delta or p95 latency >2x baseline for 5m.

nisha_pm: For prioritization at roadmap review: propose we milestone BGP GA only after 3 paying customers pass the GA checklist. Beta opens to 10 pilot customers. Thoughts?

maria_s: Sounds reasonable. Also include legal checklist for cross‑border data egress & audit logs retention — product needs to surface these constraints in the contract.

alex_k: I'll add a short YAML snippet to PRD for the acceptance suite so eng can run it in CI:

```yaml
acceptance_suite:
  - name: controlplane-reachable
    check: curl https://controlplane.example/health || exit 1
  - name: egress-ip-check
    check: nc -z $EGRESS_IP 443
  - name: cert-rotation
    check: ./scripts/rotate-cert-test.sh $CUSTOMER
```

chris_net: Can we also enumerate rollback playbooks per failure mode? E.g., BGP flap -> revert to NAT tunnel + notify customer + disable advertising.

sam_devops: I'll draft the rollback workflows and share by EOD. Will include automation hooks for failing fast.

deploy-bot: New draft PR created: github.com/redwood/inference/ops/playbooks/onprem-handshake-draft (PR #148)

alex_k: Great — please review PR and add comments on the acceptance tests. I want this baked into the PRD before roadmap signoff tomorrow. :clock1:

nisha_pm: I'll prioritize in the roadmap doc and link the PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
